record.context_brief: Natural Rayleigh-type class with log-concave diagonal coefficients
record.original_question:
Describe, in terms of Rayleigh-type correlations, a natural class RN_n
of multi-affine polynomials in n variables with
nonnegative coefficients such that whenever f belongs to RN_n and
Δ(f)(t) = Σ_{k=0}^n (n choose k) c_k t^k is the
diagonal specialization of f, the coefficient sequence (c_k) is
log-concave with no internal zeros.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A polynomial $f \in \mathbb{R}[z_1,\dots,z_n]$ is called multi-affine if it has degree at most 1 in each variable. For a multi-affine polynomial $f$ with nonnegative coefficients, its diagonal specialization is the univariate polynomial
$$\Delta(f)(t) := f(t,t,\dots,t) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k} c_k\, t^k,$$
where the coefficients $c_k \ge 0$ are read off relative to the binomial normalization. A finite sequence $(c_0,c_1,\dots,c_n)$ of nonnegative reals is called log-concave with no internal zeros if $c_k^2 \ge c_{k-1} c_{k+1}$ for $1 \le k \le n-1$ and the set $\{k : c_k > 0\}$ is an interval of integers.

A multi-affine polynomial $f$ with nonnegative coefficients is said to be (1-)Rayleigh if for every pair of distinct indices $i \ne j$ and every assignment of nonnegative real values to the remaining variables, one has
$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial z_i}\cdot \frac{\partial f}{\partial z_j} \;\ge\; f\cdot \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial z_i \partial z_j}.$$
More generally one may consider various strengthenings or weakenings of this inequality (e.g. strongly Rayleigh, almost Rayleigh, or weighted versions), collectively referred to as Rayleigh-type correlation conditions.

Problem. Identify and describe, purely in terms of Rayleigh-type correlation inequalities, a natural class $\mathrm{RN}_n$ of multi-affine polynomials in $n$ variables with nonnegative coefficients such that, for every $f \in \mathrm{RN}_n$, the coefficient sequence $(c_0,c_1,\dots,c_n)$ of its diagonal specialization $\Delta(f)$ is log-concave with no internal zeros.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any specific resolution of this problem (identifying a natural Rayleigh-type class whose diagonal specialization is automatically log-concave with no internal zeros). Related developments such as the theory of Lorentzian polynomials by Brändén–Huh and completely log-concave polynomials by Anari et al. yield log-concavity for stable/strongly Rayleigh multi-affine polynomials, but no single source was located that explicitly addresses the requested characterization in Rayleigh-correlation terms. Status is therefore recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Lorentzian Polynomials — Brändén and Huh
status_evidence.snippet: Lorentzian polynomials yield strong log-concavity of coefficient sequences for homogeneous polynomials with M-convex support.
status_evidence.claim: Lorentzian polynomial theory provides log-concavity for related classes but does not phrase the result in Rayleigh-correlation terms.

status_evidence.title: Log-Concave Polynomials II (Anari et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Completely log-concave polynomials and matroid base generating polynomials, which are strongly Rayleigh, have log-concave projections.
status_evidence.claim: Strongly Rayleigh multi-affine polynomials are known to have log-concave diagonal specializations, but a precise minimal Rayleigh-type class achieving log-concavity with no internal zeros is not pinpointed.
